titulo: Pillar page and question pages with a direct answer
lead: A pillar page is the long page that covers a central topic of your business. Around it, question pages each answer one question, starting with the answer. It's not an AI trick: it's respect for people who arrived with a question. And the questions section at the end stays useful to the reader, even without the showcase Google removed in 2026.
objetivo: write a question page with a direct answer at the top, sections shaped as questions, and a visible FAQ, without promising a rich result.

aprende.t: The difference between a pillar page and a question page
The skeleton of a question page
FAQ in 2026: useful to the reader, no showcase
The swap test against generic text

hero_alt: A bright library with a large open reference book and question cards pinned to a corkboard around it.

secoes.titulo: A pillar page in the center, questions around it

nos.detalhe: One page per central topic (2 or 3 on the whole site), long: the inemaSEO method says 2,500 to 4,000 words. It links to all the question pages on the topic and to the other pillar pages.
Each one answers one intent from your cluster (lesson 3). Short enough to solve it, long enough to bring your first-hand data.
The page starts by answering, with no "in this article we will." Someone who arrived through the question reads the answer in seconds and decides whether they want the detail.
The section headings (h2) are the reader's next questions: "how long does it take?", "what goes wrong?". It makes skimming easier.

Questions coming from search or from your community, answered on the page itself. The FAQ rich result stopped appearing on Google on 05/07/2026: the FAQPage markup no longer gives you a showcase, and the value is in the answers themselves.

secoes.legenda: Answer first, first-hand data in the middle, real questions at the end.

texto: Write the answer the way you'd tell a customer at the counter. Then cut whatever doesn't answer.
A short answer is clarity for the reader. No source shows an exact length as a factor for AI.
Right after that, what only you have: the test you ran, your business's numbers, a customer's case (with permission), the mistake you made.
With a link to the evidence: repository, product page, course, photo.
List the follow-up questions the reader would ask and use them as section headings. The cluster variations go here.
Page title up to 60 characters and description between 110 and 160.
Three or more real questions answered, if they exist. If they don't, no FAQ: making up questions is padding.
Links to the pillar page, 2 to 4 sister pages, and 2 catalog items (lesson 6).

exemplo.texto: Pillar pages 2 and 3 and the JARVIS question page were published on 09/24/2026; the pillar drafts were about 3,150 and 2,450 words.

secoes.titulo: The skeleton, the request to the agent, and the swap test
secoes.sub: The agent from your subscription writes the draft by reading your real material; you review it.

abas.html:
The FAQ rich result stopped appearing on Google on 05/07/2026, and its documentation was removed on 06/12/2026. Anyone selling FAQPage as a showcase is selling the past.

Visible questions are still useful to readers. The markup, if you keep it, has to match the text on the page.

Google's AI features guide (May 2026) says there is no special optimization to appear in AI Overviews and AI Mode, no special schema, and that you can ignore content "chunking".

What it highlights is non-commodity content: your own point of view, direct experience. That's the "How I know this" section.

• Rambling intro before the answer.
  • Made-up FAQ just to "have an FAQ".
  • A paragraph that passes the swap test: it fits any site, so it isn't yours.

secoes.sub: Use a GO group from lesson 3.

exercicios.texto: Write (or ask the agent and review) a question page using the skeleton, with your first-hand data and the evidence link.
exercicios.pronto: the answer is 2 to 4 sentences at the top, there is a section with your data and link, and no [FALTA DADO] was left unresolved.

exercicios.texto: Apply the swap test to every paragraph and rewrite the generic ones.
exercicios.pronto: you marked each paragraph as "yours" or "rewritten", and none stays true with the word swapped.

secoes.sub: The explanation shows up after your answer.

perguntas.p: Why does the question page start with the answer?
opcoes: Because it's the technique that guarantees AI citation.
Because it's clarity: someone who arrived with the question gets it resolved in seconds.
perguntas.explica: It's clarity for the reader. No source supports answer length as an AI factor; Google says there is no special optimization.

perguntas.p: A consultant promises a "FAQ showcase on Google" with FAQPage markup. In 2026...
opcoes: The FAQ rich result stopped appearing on 05/07/2026; the questions are worth only their content.
perguntas.explica: The showcase is over. Real, visible questions are still useful to the reader.

perguntas.p: You swap "bakery" for "pizzeria" and the paragraph is still true. What do you do?
opcoes: Rewrite it with your own data: the paragraph is generic.
perguntas.explica: It's the swap test. A paragraph that fits any business is commodity.

perguntas.p: There are no real questions about the topic yet. What about the FAQ?
opcoes: Go without an FAQ until there are real questions.
Copy the FAQ from another page of yours.
perguntas.explica: A made-up or copied FAQ was part of the problem with INEMA's thin listing pages (identical FAQ on all of them).

itens.texto: One long pillar page per core topic; one page per question around it.
Answer at the top, first-hand data with a link, sections phrased as questions.
If the paragraph fits any site, rewrite it.
A short answer is clarity, not an AI technique. The FAQ rich result ended on 05/07/2026; a visible FAQ is still useful to the reader.
